claims.sentence: Recent systems take the cited work, retrieved automatically or supplied by the user, locate candidate evidence in it and judge whether it supports the claim \citep{haan2025semanticcite,mocan2026refverifier,sadeghi2026deepsciverify,lee2026reflens,li2026bibagent}; some add a partial-support verdict \citep{haan2025semanticcite,mocan2026refverifier}.
claims.claim: DeepSciVerify retrieves the cited work, extracts relevant passages and judges whether they support the claim.
claims.excerpt: it retrieves the complete paper when available, extracts relevant passages using RAGbased passage retrieval, and produces a final verdict from passage-level evidence.
claims.note: Supported for the clause it is cited for. Its label set is SUPPORTS / CONTRADICTS / NEI, and it is correctly not cited for the partial-support clause.

claims.sentence: Locating the passage is harder in full text than in an abstract: RefVerifier's evidence-localization hit rate was 98\% on abstracts and 68\% on complete papers \citep{mocan2026refverifier}, and in one small evaluation, naively adding full-text evidence changed verifier accuracy only modestly, which the authors suggest reflects the difficulty of selecting the most informative passages \citep{sadeghi2026deepsciverify}.
claims.claim: In one small evaluation, naively adding full-text evidence changed verifier accuracy only modestly, which the authors suggest reflects the difficulty of selecting the most informative passages.
claims.excerpt: Providing access to full-text evidence improves most models, indicating that information beyond the abstract can be useful. However, the gains from naive full-text usage are limited: GPT-4 decreases from 82.2 to 81.3 Micro-F1, while Claude Sonnet 4.6 improves only marginally from 81.1 to 82.4. ... Since SC I TANCE uses a 91-instance test split, these gains should be interpreted with appropriate caution ... while naively providing full-text documents leads to only modest improvements (Section 6.3). This suggests that the challenge is not only retrieving more information, but selecting the parts of the document most informative for the claim.
claims.note: Supported. Context only: the metric is Micro-F1 (equal to accuracy for single-label classification); 'changed' correctly covers GPT-4's small drop alongside small gains; the source says the challenge is 'not only' retrieval but selection, which the manuscript's 'suggest reflects' does not overstate. The staged DeepSciVerify pipeline, which also uses full text selectively, gains +4.5 Micro-F1, so 'naively' is the necessary qualifier.
